```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r readModelDb("Abbas_2020_sertraline_ddQTcF")()$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/cpdd.749>

Abbas et al. (2020) report the thorough-QT study of sertraline, a selective
serotonin reuptake inhibitor. Healthy adults received, in a randomized
3-period crossover, sertraline titrated over a week to a supratherapeutic
400 mg/day (200 mg twice daily), matching placebo, and a single open-label dose
of moxifloxacin 400 mg as the positive control. ECGs and plasma samples were
taken on day 1 (after the first 50 mg dose) and on day 14 (after the last
200 mg morning dose, at steady state).

The exposure-response analysis is a linear mixed-effects model (R `nlme::lme`,
REML) of the change from baseline in the Fridericia-corrected QT interval:

DeltaQTc_ijk = (mu + TRT_j + t_k + eta_mu,i) + theta0 (BQTc_i - Bbar) +
(theta1 + eta_C,i) C_ijk + eps_ijk

fitted separately for sertraline and for its principal metabolite
N-desmethylsertraline. The paper prints only the two slopes (0.036 ms per
ng/mL for each analyte). It also prints three model predictions of the
placebo-corrected effect DeltaDeltaQTcF for sertraline and draws the population
regression line of DeltaQTcF on concentration for each analyte (Figure 3). The
three packaged files use exactly that information:

| Model file | Endpoint | Structure | Source |
|------------|----------|-----------|--------|
| `Abbas_2020_sertraline_ddQTcF` | DeltaDeltaQTcF (ms) | `e0 + slope * C` | slope from Results; `e0` back-solved from the three Results predictions |
| `Abbas_2020_sertraline_dQTcF` | DeltaQTcF (ms) | `e0 + slope * C` | slope from Results; `e0` digitised from Figure 3A |
| `Abbas_2020_desmethylsertraline_dQTcF` | DeltaQTcF (ms) | `e0 + slope * C` | slope from Results; `e0` digitised from Figure 3B |

`C` is `CP_SERTRALINE_NGML` or `CP_DESMETHYLSERTRALINE_NGML` (ng/mL). The paper
characterises the pharmacokinetics by non-compartmental analysis only
(Table 3), so these are PD-only models: the user supplies the concentration.
The random-effect covariance and the residual variance are not reported, so all
three are typical-value models with `addSd = fixed(0)`.

# Population

```{r population}
pop <- readModelDb("Abbas_2020_sertraline_ddQTcF")()$population
str(pop[c("n_subjects", "age_range", "weight_range", "sex_female_pct", "race_ethnicity")])
```

Fifty-four healthy adults were enrolled at a single site in Brussels (Abbas
2020 Table 2): mean age 36.5 years (range 20-54), 43 men and 11 women, 85.2%
White, mean weight 74.4 kg and BMI 24.8 kg/m^2. The PK/PD data set held 1066
sertraline-QTcF pairs and 1050 QTcF records on placebo, from days 1 and 14.

# Source trace

| Quantity | Value | Source |
|----------|-------|--------|
| Model equation | linear mixed effects, random intercept and slope | Methods 'Pharmacokinetic/Pharmacodynamic Analysis' |
| Sertraline slope | 0.036 ms per ng/mL (90% CI 0.029-0.043) | Results 'Pharmacokinetic/Pharmacodynamic Analysis'; Abstract |
| N-desmethylsertraline slope | 0.036 ms per ng/mL (90% CI 0.029-0.042) | Results 'Pharmacokinetic/Pharmacodynamic Analysis' |
| DeltaDeltaQTcF predictions | 3.57 ms at 86 ng/mL; 8.93 ms at 234 ng/mL; 8.55 ms at 223.5 ng/mL | Results 'Pharmacokinetic/Pharmacodynamic Analysis' |
| DeltaDeltaQTcF intercept `e0` | 0.49 ms | back-solved from the three predictions (below) |
| DeltaQTcF intercept, sertraline | -5.9 ms | digitised from Figure 3A |
| DeltaQTcF intercept, N-desmethylsertraline | -6.4 ms | digitised from Figure 3B |
| Time-matched DeltaDeltaQTcF, day 14 | 5.597-9.651 ms | Table 4 |
| Day 1 and day 14 NCA | Cmax, Tmax, AUC24, Cmin | Table 3 |
| Random effects, residual error | not reported | typical-value models, `addSd = fixed(0)` |

```{r load-models}
mod_dd <- readModelDb("Abbas_2020_sertraline_ddQTcF")
mod_d <- readModelDb("Abbas_2020_sertraline_dQTcF")
mod_dm <- readModelDb("Abbas_2020_desmethylsertraline_dQTcF")

# Typical-value prediction at a vector of concentrations. The models are
# algebraic, so all rows sit in one subject at successive solver times.
predict_qtc <- function(mod, conc, conc_col = "CP_SERTRALINE_NGML") {
  ev <- data.frame(id = 1L, time = seq_along(conc), evid = 0L, amt = 0)
  ev[[conc_col]] <- conc
  as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = ev))$QTcF
}
```

## Back-solving the DeltaDeltaQTcF intercept

The Methods equation contains an intercept, treatment and nominal-time effects
and a baseline term, none of which is printed. In the placebo-corrected contrast
(sertraline minus placebo at the same time point) everything but the treatment
effect TRT and the concentration term cancels, so DeltaDeltaQTcF = TRT +
slope * C. The Results print that prediction at three concentrations. At the
printed slope each anchor implies its own intercept:

```{r backsolve}
anchors <- data.frame(
  label = c("mean therapeutic Cmax", "10 ms upper-bound crossing", "day 14 mean Cmax"),
  conc = c(86, 223.5, 234),
  pred = c(3.57, 8.55, 8.93)
)
anchors$e0_implied <- anchors$pred - 0.036 * anchors$conc
unrounded <- stats::coef(stats::lm(pred ~ conc, data = anchors))
knitr::kable(
  anchors |>
    dplyr::mutate(e0_implied = round(e0_implied, 4)) |>
    dplyr::rename(
      "Anchor" = label, "Concentration (ng/mL)" = conc,
      "Printed DeltaDeltaQTcF (ms)" = pred, "Implied e0 at slope 0.036 (ms)" = e0_implied
    ),
  caption = "Intercepts implied by the three Abbas 2020 predictions at the printed slope."
)
unrounded
stopifnot(
  # The implied intercepts span 0.032 ms, so the packaged 0.49 (their
  # centre) misses no anchor by more than 0.016 ms.
  diff(range(anchors$e0_implied)) < 0.035,
  # The unrounded line through the anchors has a slope that rounds to the
  # printed 0.036, so the spread is the rounding of the printed slope.
  round(unrounded[["conc"]], 3) == 0.036,
  max(abs(stats::residuals(stats::lm(pred ~ conc, data = anchors)))) < 0.005
)
```

No single intercept reproduces all three predictions to their 0.005 ms rounding
at the printed slope, but the unrounded line (slope
`r signif(unrounded[["conc"]], 4)` ms per ng/mL, intercept
`r signif(unrounded[["(Intercept)"]], 3)` ms) does, and its slope rounds to the
printed 0.036. The Figure 3A regression line, digitised independently below,
has the same 0.0362 slope. The spread is therefore the rounding of the printed
slope. The packaged model keeps the printed slope and uses the centre of the
implied intercepts, 0.49 ms.

# Virtual cohort

No stochastic cohort is simulated for the QTc models. The paper reports neither
the random-effect covariance nor the residual error, so the packaged models are
typical-value models and a stochastic cohort would add no information. The
concentration driver later in this article does use a simulated cohort.

# Simulation and validation gate: the Results predictions

```{r results-gate}
gate <- anchors |>
  dplyr::select(conc, pred) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    model = predict_qtc(mod_dd, conc),
    diff = model - pred,
    # Half a unit in the third decimal of the slope, times the
    # concentration, plus the rounding of the printed prediction.
    tolerance = 5e-4 * conc + 0.005
  )
gate |>
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(c(model, diff, tolerance), ~ round(.x, 3))) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Concentration (ng/mL)" = conc, "Paper (ms)" = pred,
    "Packaged model (ms)" = model, "Difference (ms)" = diff,
    "Rounding tolerance (ms)" = tolerance
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Replicates the DeltaDeltaQTcF predictions in the Results of Abbas 2020.")
stopifnot(all(abs(gate$diff) <= gate$tolerance), max(abs(gate$diff)) < 0.02)
```

All three predictions are reproduced to within 0.016 ms. The paper also
states that, by this model, the sertraline concentration has to exceed about
2.6 times the 86 ng/mL therapeutic Cmax (223.5 ng/mL) before the upper 90%
confidence bound crosses 10 ms; the confidence bound needs the parameter
covariance, which is not printed, so only the point prediction is checked.

# Replicate published figures

## Figure 3 -- DeltaQTcF against concentration

```{r fig3, fig.cap = "Replicates the regression lines of Figure 3 of Abbas 2020: DeltaQTcF against sertraline (A) and N-desmethylsertraline (B) concentration. Points are the line read from the figure by the maintainers at 100 ng/mL steps."}
# Line positions read from the solid red line of Figure 3, at the
# 100 ng/mL gridlines (ms).
fig3_dig <- data.frame(
  analyte = rep(c("A: sertraline", "B: N-desmethylsertraline"), c(6, 5)),
  conc = c(0, 100, 200, 300, 400, 500, 0, 100, 200, 300, 400),
  qtc = c(-5.9, -2.3, 1.3, 5.0, 8.6, 12.2, -6.4, -2.9, 0.7, 4.2, 7.8)
)
grid_s <- seq(0, 525, by = 5)
grid_m <- seq(0, 450, by = 5)
fig3_mod <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  data.frame(analyte = "A: sertraline", conc = grid_s, qtc = predict_qtc(mod_d, grid_s)),
  data.frame(
    analyte = "B: N-desmethylsertraline", conc = grid_m,
    qtc = predict_qtc(mod_dm, grid_m, "CP_DESMETHYLSERTRALINE_NGML")
  )
)
ggplot(fig3_mod, aes(conc, qtc)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey60") +
  geom_line(colour = "firebrick") +
  geom_point(data = fig3_dig, shape = 1, size = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~analyte, ncol = 1, scales = "free_x") +
  labs(x = "Plasma concentration (ng/mL)", y = "Change from baseline in QTcF (ms)") +
  theme_bw()

fig3_chk <- fig3_dig |>
  dplyr::left_join(fig3_mod, by = c("analyte", "conc"), suffix = c("_fig", "_model"))
stopifnot(max(abs(fig3_chk$qtc_fig - fig3_chk$qtc_model)) < 0.4)
```

The packaged lines run within a pixel (0.23 ms) of the published lines at zero
concentration, where the intercepts were read, and diverge by at most
`r round(max(abs(fig3_chk$qtc_fig - fig3_chk$qtc_model)), 2)` ms at the far end
because the packaged slope is the printed 0.036 rather than the line's own
0.0362 (sertraline) or 0.0356 (N-desmethylsertraline).

## Figure 4A and Table 4 -- the day 14 time course

Figure 4A overlays the mean day-14 sertraline concentration on the time-matched
DeltaDeltaQTcF. Evaluating the DeltaDeltaQTcF model at the mean concentration of
each time point and comparing it with the Table 4 least-squares mean
differences shows the "proteresis" the authors describe: the observed effect
peaks at 4 h while the concentration peaks at 8 h.

```{r fig4a, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 4A of Abbas 2020 with the model overlay: day 14 time-matched DeltaDeltaQTcF (Table 4, points with 90% CI) and the DeltaDeltaQTcF model evaluated at the mean sertraline concentration of each time point (line)."}
# Mean day-14 sertraline concentration read from Figure 4A by the
# maintainers (ng/mL); the 4 h value 213 matches the printed 213.1.
fig4_conc <- data.frame(
  time = c(0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 12, 24, 48, 72),
  conc = c(193, 190, 199, 207, 213, 220, 234, 240, 205, 147, 90, 59)
)
table4 <- data.frame(
  time = c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 12, 24),
  ddqtc = c(6.957, 7.851, 7.824, 9.651, 7.377, 6.511, 5.597, 5.677, 7.346),
  lo = c(4.942, 5.835, 5.808, 7.635, 5.362, 4.495, 3.582, 3.662, 5.331),
  hi = c(8.973, 9.866, 9.840, 11.666, 9.393, 8.526, 7.613, 7.693, 9.360)
)
fig4_conc$model <- predict_qtc(mod_dd, fig4_conc$conc)
ggplot() +
  geom_line(data = fig4_conc, aes(time, model), colour = "firebrick") +
  geom_pointrange(data = table4, aes(time, ddqtc, ymin = lo, ymax = hi), colour = "steelblue") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 10, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  labs(x = "Hours after the day 14 dose", y = "DeltaDeltaQTcF (ms)") +
  theme_bw()

t4 <- table4 |> dplyr::left_join(fig4_conc, by = "time")
t4 |>
  dplyr::mutate(diff = round(model - ddqtc, 2), model = round(model, 2)) |>
  dplyr::select(time, conc, ddqtc, model, diff) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Time (h)" = time, "Mean sertraline (ng/mL)" = conc,
    "Table 4 DeltaDeltaQTcF (ms)" = ddqtc, "Model at mean conc (ms)" = model,
    "Model - Table 4 (ms)" = diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Model at the Figure 4A mean concentrations against the Abbas 2020 Table 4 time-matched least-squares mean differences.")
stopifnot(
  # The concentration-driven prediction tracks the time-matched
  # estimates on average; the hour-to-hour pattern is the proteresis the
  # paper describes and the model has no term for.
  abs(mean(t4$model - t4$ddqtc)) < 1.5,
  max(abs(t4$model - t4$ddqtc)) < 4
)
```

Averaged over the nine time points the model is within
`r round(abs(mean(t4$model - t4$ddqtc)), 2)` ms of Table 4. The model, a
direct-effect linear function of concentration, cannot reproduce the
early peak at 4 h (Table 4: 9.65 ms against a model value of
`r round(t4$model[t4$time == 4], 2)` ms) or the dip at 8 h; the authors attribute
part of the pattern to a meal at about 4 h.

# Driving the models from a dose

The QTc models need a sertraline concentration at each ECG time. Abbas 2020 has
no population PK model, so here the concentration comes from
`Zhang_2024_sertraline`, a one-compartment model fitted to trough samples from
Chinese psychiatric inpatients, run through the titration schedule of Table 1.
Age is drawn from the reported mean and SD, truncated to the reported range.
This is an illustration of how the PD models are used, not a test of them.

```{r pk-sim, message = FALSE}
n_sub <- 100
pk_mod <- readModelDb("Zhang_2024_sertraline")

# Table 1: 50 mg on day 1; 50 mg BID day 2; 50 mg am / 100 mg pm day 3;
# 100 mg BID days 4-5; 100 mg am / 200 mg pm day 6; 200 mg BID days 7-13;
# 200 mg am only on day 14. Doses 12 h apart; day 1 dose at time 0.
dose_tbl <- data.frame(
  time = c(0, 24, 36, 48, 60, 72, 84, 96, 108, 120, 132, seq(144, 300, by = 12), 312),
  amt = c(50, 50, 50, 50, 100, 100, 100, 100, 100, 100, 200, rep(200, 14), 200)
)
obs_times <- sort(unique(c(
  0, 0.5, 1:8, 10, 12, 16, 20, 24,
  312 + c(0, 0.5, 1:8, 10, 12, 16, 20, 24, 36, 48, 60, 72)
)))

set.seed(20200301)
age <- pmin(pmax(rnorm(n_sub, 36.5, 9.7), 20), 54)
pk_events <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  merge(data.frame(id = seq_len(n_sub)), dose_tbl |> dplyr::mutate(evid = 1L, cmt = "depot"), by = NULL),
  merge(data.frame(id = seq_len(n_sub)), data.frame(time = obs_times, amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central"), by = NULL)
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(AGE = age[id]) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))

pk_sim <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(pk_mod, events = pk_events, returnType = "data.frame")) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc)
```

## PKNCA on the driving concentrations

```{r pknca}
pk_nca <- pk_sim |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(treatment = "sertraline")
conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(pk_nca, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(
  merge(data.frame(id = seq_len(n_sub), treatment = "sertraline"), dose_tbl, by = NULL),
  amt ~ time | treatment + id
)
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = c(0, 312), end = c(24, 336),
  cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE, cmin = c(FALSE, TRUE)
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

sim_long <- as.data.frame(nca_res$result) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "tmax", "auclast", "cmin")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(day = ifelse(start == 0, "Day 1 (50 mg)", "Day 14 (200 mg, 400 mg/day)")) |>
  dplyr::select(day, PPTESTCD, PPORRES)
# Abbas 2020 Table 3: geometric means (Cmax, AUC24, Cmin) and median tmax.
ref_tbl <- data.frame(
  day = c("Day 1 (50 mg)", "Day 14 (200 mg, 400 mg/day)"),
  cmax = c(11.39, 234.2),
  tmax = c(5.06, 7.15),
  auclast = c(154.3, 4388),
  cmin = c(NA, 135.3)
)
cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = sim_long,
  reference = ref_tbl,
  by = "day",
  units = c(cmax = "ng/mL", tmax = "h", auclast = "ng*h/mL", cmin = "ng/mL"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Simulated median NCA (Zhang 2024 PK driver) against Abbas 2020 Table 3. AUC0-24 is reported as AUClast over the 0-24 h interval.")
```

```{r pknca-footnote, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
if (!is.null(attr(cmp, "footnote"))) cat(attr(cmp, "footnote"), "\n")
```

At day 14 steady state, where the QTc models are applied, the driver lands
close to Table 3 (Cmax, Cmin and AUC0-24 within about 15%). After the first
50 mg dose it over-predicts exposure about two- to three-fold with a late Tmax.
The Zhang 2024 model was fitted to trough concentrations in patients and fixes
its absorption rate constant (0.098 1/h) from the literature, so the
single-dose absorption phase is not something it can describe. The flagged rows
reflect the PK driver, not the QTc models. A user with observed or
better-matched concentrations should supply those instead.

## Predicted day 14 DeltaDeltaQTcF from the driver

```{r driven-qtc, fig.cap = "DeltaDeltaQTcF over the day 14 dosing interval predicted from the Zhang 2024 sertraline concentrations (median and 5th-95th percentile band over the simulated cohort), with the Abbas 2020 Table 4 estimates (points)."}
d14 <- pk_sim |>
  dplyr::filter(time >= 312, time <= 336) |>
  dplyr::mutate(tad = time - 312)
d14$QTcF <- predict_qtc(mod_dd, d14$Cc)
d14 |>
  dplyr::group_by(tad) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    med = stats::median(QTcF), lo = stats::quantile(QTcF, 0.05),
    hi = stats::quantile(QTcF, 0.95), .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(tad, med)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), fill = "firebrick", alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_line(colour = "firebrick") +
  geom_point(data = table4, aes(time, ddqtc), colour = "steelblue") +
  labs(x = "Hours after the day 14 dose", y = "DeltaDeltaQTcF (ms)") +
  theme_bw()
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Typical-value models only.** Abbas 2020 does not print the random-effect
  covariance (random intercept and slope, unstructured) or the residual
  variance. No etas are declared and `addSd` is `fixed(0)`. The sample-size
  assumption of 5.36 ms intrasubject variability (Methods 'Statistical
  Analysis') is a design input, not a model estimate, and is not used.
* **DeltaDeltaQTcF intercept back-solved.** `e0 = 0.49` ms is the centre of the
  intercepts implied by the three printed predictions at the printed slope; it
  is the sertraline treatment effect TRT of the Methods equation. The printed
  slope is kept; the unrounded line (slope 0.03622) reproduces the predictions
  exactly.
* **DeltaQTcF intercepts digitised.** The intercepts of the two change-from-baseline
  models were read by the maintainers from the regression lines of Figure 3,
  calibrated on the figure gridlines (one pixel is 0.23 ms). They are population
  averages over the unprinted intercept, treatment, nominal-time and baseline
  terms, so the change-from-baseline files reproduce the regression line, not a
  time-specific prediction.
* **No placebo-corrected metabolite model.** The paper prints no prediction for
  N-desmethylsertraline, so its treatment effect cannot be recovered and only the
  change-from-baseline form is packaged.
* **Concentration driver.** The PK simulation uses `Zhang_2024_sertraline`
  (patients, trough data) because Abbas 2020 reports NCA only. Its mismatch with
  Table 3 is a property of that model in this population.
* **No errata** were found for this article (Crossref and Europe PMC, checked
  2026-11-27). The single supplementary file is a heart-rate figure (Figure S1)
  that holds no model parameters.
